source_text.indications: For the temporary relief of minor aches and pains and for the reduction of fever.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Nausea, stomach discomfort and skin rash are reported. Serious skin reactions and allergic reactions are uncommon but possible.
source_text.warnings: Contains acetaminophen. Severe liver damage may occur if more than the labelled amount is taken, if taken with other medicines containing acetaminophen, or if taken with alcohol. Ask a doctor before use if you have liver disease.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if a skin reaction such as redness, blisters or rash appears, if pain or fever gets worse or lasts more than a few days, or if new symptoms appear.

source_text.indications: For the temporary relief of minor aches and pains, including headache. Caffeine is included to increase the pain-relieving effect of the analgesic.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Nausea, nervousness, restlessness, difficulty sleeping and a faster heartbeat are reported with the caffeine component.
source_text.warnings: Contains acetaminophen and caffeine. Limit other sources of caffeine such as tea, coffee and cola while taking this product. Severe liver damage may occur if more than the labelled amount of acetaminophen is taken or if it is taken with alcohol.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if nervousness, sleeplessness or a rapid heartbeat occurs, if a skin reaction appears, or if pain lasts more than a few days.

source_text.indications: For the temporary relief of minor aches and pains due to headache, toothache, backache, muscular aches, menstrual cramps and minor pain of arthritis, and for reduction of fever.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea and dizziness are common. Stomach bleeding and ulcers can occur, sometimes without warning.
source_text.warnings: Contains a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug. Risk of severe stomach bleeding is higher in people over 60, people who have had stomach ulcers or bleeding, people taking blood thinners or steroids, and people who drink alcohol. May cause kidney problems and raise blood pressure. Ask a doctor before use if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, kidney disease, asthma or are pregnant.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if you have stomach pain that does not go away, vomit blood, pass black or bloody stools, have swelling of the face or difficulty breathing, or if pain or fever lasts longer than a few days.

source_text.indications: For the temporary relief of minor aches, pains and fever, combining an anti-inflammatory pain reliever with a fever reducer.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Stomach pain, heartburn, nausea and dizziness are reported. Stomach bleeding and ulcers can occur with the anti-inflammatory component.
source_text.warnings: Contains both a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug and acetaminophen. Do not take other products containing either ingredient at the same time. Risk of stomach bleeding is higher with alcohol, blood thinners, steroids or a past ulcer. Ask a doctor before use if you have heart, kidney or liver disease, high blood pressure or asthma.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if stomach pain persists, if you notice blood in vomit or stools, if a skin rash or facial swelling appears, or if symptoms last more than a few days.

source_text.indications: Temporarily relieves symptoms due to hay fever or other upper respiratory allergies: runny nose, sneezing, itchy and watery eyes, and itching of the nose or throat. Also used for hives.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Drowsiness, tiredness, dry mouth and headache are common. Drowsiness is more likely at higher than labelled amounts.
source_text.warnings: May cause drowsiness; be careful when driving or operating machinery, and avoid alcohol and other sedatives. Ask a doctor before use if you have liver or kidney disease, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if an allergic reaction occurs, if hives are accompanied by difficulty breathing or swallowing or swelling of the tongue, or if symptoms do not improve within a few days.

source_text.indications: Relieves symptoms of allergic rhinitis such as sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes and nasal itching, and relieves itching due to chronic hives.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Sleepiness, tiredness, dry mouth and nasal irritation are reported. Children may show fever or cough.
source_text.warnings: May cause sleepiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you, and avoid alcohol. Ask a doctor before use if you have kidney disease, are pregnant or are breastfeeding.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if you have difficulty passing urine, if an allergic reaction occurs, or if symptoms do not improve.

source_text.indications: Temporarily relieves cough due to minor throat and bronchial irritation, along with sneezing, runny nose and watery eyes due to the common cold or allergy.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Marked drowsiness, dizziness, dry mouth, nose and throat, blurred vision and excitability in children are reported.
source_text.warnings: May cause marked drowsiness; alcohol, sedatives and tranquillisers increase this. Be careful when driving or operating machinery. Do not use for a persistent or chronic cough such as occurs with smoking, asthma or emphysema. Ask a doctor before use if you have glaucoma, a breathing problem, an enlarged prostate or difficulty passing urine.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if the cough lasts more than seven days, comes back, or is accompanied by fever, rash or a persistent headache.

source_text.indications: Used as a mucolytic to loosen thick mucus in the airways so that a productive cough clears more easily, in respiratory conditions with excess sticky secretions.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Nausea, altered taste, mouth or throat numbness, stomach upset and diarrhoea are reported. Allergic skin reactions are uncommon.
source_text.warnings: Ask a doctor before use if you have a stomach ulcer, impaired kidney or liver function, or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. Severe skin reactions have been reported rarely.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and see a doctor if a skin rash, blistering or swelling of the face or throat appears, or if the cough does not improve within a few days.

source_text.indications: A dietary supplement used to prevent and treat vitamin D deficiency, and to support calcium absorption for bone health.
source_text.adverse_reactions: At excessive intake, nausea, vomiting, weakness, frequent urination, constipation and raised blood calcium can occur.
source_text.warnings: Too much vitamin D can be harmful. Ask a doctor before use if you have kidney disease, high blood calcium, sarcoidosis or are taking other supplements containing vitamin D or calcium. Blood levels should be checked by a doctor rather than guessed.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and see a doctor if you have persistent nausea or vomiting, weakness, confusion, bone pain or a large increase in thirst and urination.

source_text.indications: A dietary supplement used to support bone health where dietary calcium and vitamin D are insufficient, including in osteoporosis management under medical advice.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Constipation, gas, bloating and stomach upset are common.
source_text.warnings: Ask a doctor before use if you have kidney stones, kidney disease, high blood calcium or parathyroid disease. Calcium can reduce the absorption of some medicines, including thyroid medicines and some antibiotics, so spacing them apart matters — ask your pharmacist.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and see a doctor if you have severe constipation, stomach pain, nausea and vomiting, or symptoms of a kidney stone such as pain in the side and blood in the urine.

source_text.indications: A supplement used to prevent and treat iron-deficiency anaemia and folate deficiency, including during pregnancy under medical advice.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Constipation, dark or black stools, nausea, stomach cramps and a metallic taste are common. Dark stools are expected and harmless.
source_text.warnings: Accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under six; keep out of reach of children. Ask a doctor before use if you have a condition that causes iron overload, a stomach ulcer or inflammatory bowel disease. Tea, coffee, calcium and antacids reduce iron absorption.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and see a doctor if you have severe stomach pain, vomiting, blood in the stool, or if tiredness does not improve after the course your doctor advised.

source_text.indications: A first-aid antiseptic applied to the skin to help prevent infection in minor cuts, scrapes and burns.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Skin irritation, redness, itching and staining of the skin are reported. Allergic skin reactions are uncommon.
source_text.warnings: For external use only. Do not use in the eyes, over large areas of the body, on deep or puncture wounds, serious burns or animal bites. Ask a doctor before use if you have a thyroid disorder or are allergic to iodine. Do not bandage tightly.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if the condition worsens, if redness, swelling or discharge increases, or if it does not improve within seven days.

source_text.indications: An antifungal cream used on the skin to treat athlete’s foot, jock itch, ringworm and other fungal skin infections.
source_text.adverse_reactions: Burning, stinging, redness, peeling and itching at the application site are reported.
source_text.warnings: For external use only. Do not use in the eyes. Ask a doctor before use for a child under two years, or for infections on the scalp or nails, which need a doctor.
source_text.stop_use: Stop use and ask a doctor if irritation occurs or gets worse, or if there is no improvement within four weeks for athlete’s foot or two weeks for other fungal skin infections.
